title: How to Use Google Gemini Spark to Automate Everyday Tasks
excerpt: Google's Spark agent can summarise email, log leads and work across Workspace apps in the background. Here is who can use it, how to set up a task, and where to keep a human check.
body:
• Gemini Spark is Google's background agent for paid users: it can work across Gmail, Docs, Calendar and Drive on instructions you write in plain language.
  • To start, open Menu, then Spark in the Gemini app, describe one clear task, attach any file it needs, and submit.
  • Check the Tasks view regularly — Spark can pause for your input, and Google warns against giving it passwords, payment details or highly sensitive jobs.
  • Reusable skills, invoked by typing a slash and the skill name, are replacing Gems as the way to repeat a routine the same way each time.

For anyone who lives inside Google's apps, the pitch is simple: hand a repetitive job to an assistant that keeps working after you close the chat. That assistant is Gemini Spark, an agentic tool Google announced in May at its I/O developer conference and now explains in a step-by-step guide covered by Engadget.

Spark is designed to take proactive action in the background, within the limits you set. Google's own examples include turning a batch of your past email replies into a guide to your writing style, keeping track of internship openings, and summarising recent mail so you can start the morning with a recap instead of a full inbox. Because it connects to Workspace apps including Gmail, Docs, Calendar and Slides, a single instruction can span several tools at once.

What Spark can do

The clearest use cases are multi-step chores that follow a pattern. In one example described in the guide, a photographer asks Spark to watch for enquiry emails, pull out the client's name and requested date, record the lead in a Sheet called a client tracker, and create a Drive folder named for that client. Nothing in that chain is technically difficult; the saving is that it happens without the owner copying details between apps each time.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=XFAlIARA5gs

Spark also works through Gemini in Chrome, where an auto browse feature can handle browser-based jobs such as restaurant reservations or travel. A related feature, Personal Intelligence, lets Gemini tailor suggestions using information from a user's Google apps.

Who can use it, and what it costs

Access is the first hurdle. Spark requires a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription, although some business subscribers may also qualify. It is not available to users located in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, the United Kingdom or Nigeria. You also need the Keep activity setting switched on, which lets you resume chats where you left off.

Spark runs in the Gemini mobile app, the Gemini Mac app and the web app. Start with a low-stakes, easily checked task — a morning email recap — rather than a workflow whose output goes straight to a client.

How to create and monitor a task

Creating a task takes three actions: open the menu and choose Spark, write the task in your own words in the text box, and submit it. If the job depends on a document, you can upload a file or attach something from Drive or a notebook at that same stage. The more specific the instruction — which emails count, what to extract, where the result should go — the easier the output is to verify.

Monitoring matters as much as setup. From Menu, then Spark, then Tasks, you can open a job's thread, make changes, and see whether Gemini is waiting on you to take over part of a task in the browser. Tapping the progress chip opens a work panel listing completed, current and planned steps.

Limits and the shift to skills

Google is explicit that this is not a set-and-forget system. AI tools can still make mistakes, including hallucinations, and the company warns users not to place sensitive information such as login or payment details in a task thread; enter those yourself on the relevant website instead. It also cautions against scheduling especially sensitive tasks to run while you are offline, when an error could go unnoticed.

The customisation layer is changing too. At the end of September, Google said skills would replace Gemini Gems as the way users store standing instructions. A skill can capture a routine such as preparing for a presentation or writing in a particular style, and can be called up by typing a forward slash followed by its name.

What it means for busy households

For diaspora professionals juggling work inboxes, family calendars and paperwork across time zones, Spark's value is practical rather than dramatic: one less recap to compile, one less lead to copy by hand, and a routine that runs the same way each time. Start small, review the first few runs in the Tasks view, and only then trust it with a workflow you would be sorry to see done badly.
